title: Word List 5 — Test rehearsal
intro: Five parts, fifty points, laid out the way the real one is. Part III asks you to write the word yourself, and Part V asks for whole sentences — those are the two that catch people out.

parts.name: Part I
parts.title: Vocabulary Matching
parts.how: Choose the letter of the best definition for each word.
defs: the way one holds the body; a pose or position
able to do many different things, or to be used in many ways
to hold back; to smother or cut off the air from
quick and sure; skillful at handling
the hiding of one heavenly body by another
to write or carve into something as a permanent record
clothes, especially fine or formal ones
working with great care and effort
not fully worked out or final; hesitating
something that covers or hides from view
to develop and change gradually over time
to please greatly; to win over by charm

parts.name: Part II
parts.title: Multiple Choice: Meaning in Context
parts.how: Choose the word that best completes each sentence.

items.q: The lake at dawn was so ______ that every cloud lay doubled in it.
items.why: Calm and peaceful. The doubled clouds are the clue — water only does that when nothing is disturbing it.

items.q: One ______ flick of the wrist sent the stone skipping four times.
items.why: Quick and sure. Diligent is about effort over time; this was one movement, done well.

items.q: Her grandmother's wedding ______ had been folded in tissue paper for forty years.
items.why: Clothes, and fine ones. Nobody keeps ordinary clothes in tissue paper for forty years.

items.q: What began as four friends in a garage would ______ into a company of two hundred.
items.why: To develop and change gradually. The sentence spans years, which is what evolve needs.

items.q: Nothing is settled yet, so the date is still ______.
items.why: Not final. “Nothing is settled yet” is the definition said another way.

items.q: A ______ of smoke hung over the valley long after the fire was out.
items.why: Something that covers or hides from view. An eclipse is one body hiding another, not smoke lying over a valley.

items.q: He had an ______ gift for mimicry that nobody had ever taught him.
items.why: Born with it. “Nobody had ever taught him” rules out anything learned.

items.q: The stonecutter was hired to ______ all forty names around the base.
items.why: To carve as a permanent record. That is what a stonecutter is for.

items.q: Years of leaning over a desk had ruined his ______.
items.why: The way he holds his body. Attire would be ruined by moths, not by leaning.

items.q: She had to ______ a yawn as the third speaker got to his feet.
items.why: To hold back. The same word covers smothering a fire and smothering a yawn.

parts.name: Part III
parts.title: Synonyms, Antonyms & Word Relationships
parts.how: Write the best vocabulary word on each line. Spelling counts.

items.q: A synonym for calm or peaceful:
items.why: Tranquil. Tranquility is the noun — the state of being tranquil — and the line asked for the describing word.

items.q: An antonym for clumsy:
items.why: Deft. Clumsy hands fumble; deft hands do not.

items.q: A synonym for hardworking:
items.why: Diligent — working with great care and effort.

items.q: An antonym for learned:
items.why: Innate. If it was not learned, it was there from birth.

items.q: A word meaning fine or formal clothing:
items.why: Attire. It can also be a verb, to dress someone up.

items.q: An antonym for definite or settled:
items.why: Tentative — not fully worked out, and ready to change.

items.q: A word meaning to carve a permanent record into stone:
items.why: Inscribe. The thing carved is an inscription.

items.q: A synonym for to charm or delight:
items.why: Captivate — to win someone over by special charm.

items.q: A word meaning able to be used in many different ways:
items.why: Versatile. The noun is versatility.

items.q: The noun form of evolve:
items.why: Evolution — the changes that take place as something evolves.

parts.name: Part IV
parts.title: Parts of Speech
parts.how: Write noun, verb, adjective or adverb for the bold word as it is used.

items.q: The whole class roared at the clown's antics.
items.why: A noun — the antics are a thing the class roared at.

items.q: Low cloud will shroud the peak until Thursday.
items.why: A verb here. Shroud is also a noun, but this sentence has the cloud doing it.

items.q: The whole valley was tranquil once the storm had passed.
items.why: An adjective — it describes the valley.

items.q: He likes to posture as an expert whenever a newcomer arrives.
items.why: A verb. Posture is usually a noun, which is exactly why this one is on the test.

items.q: The inscription over the library door is in Latin.
items.why: A noun. Inscribe is the verb; the inscription is the thing carved.

parts.name: Part V
parts.title: Application & Critical Thinking
parts.how: Answer in complete sentences, using the vocabulary word correctly.

items.q: Explain how being diligent could help someone learn a hard skill. Use diligent in your answer.
items.model: A diligent player practises carefully every day, so the hard parts get a little easier each week instead of staying hard.

items.q: Explain the difference between something innate and something learned.
items.model: An innate ability is one you are born with, and a learned ability is one you picked up by being taught or by practising.

items.q: Use shroud and tranquil together in one logical sentence.
items.model: A shroud of mist lay over the tranquil lake until the sun came up and burned it off.

items.q: Why might a tentative plan still be worth making? Use tentative in your answer.
items.model: A tentative plan gives everybody something to work from, and it can be changed later when the missing details are known.

items.q: Explain what makes a tool or a person versatile. Use versatile in your answer.
items.model: A versatile tool is useful for many different jobs, so a pocket knife is more versatile than a tool that only opens tins.
